youtube.title: Paul Revere Never Shouted "The British Are Coming"
youtube.description:
On the night of April 18, 1775, Paul Revere rode to warn rebel leaders that British troops were marching out of Boston. But shouting "the British are coming" would have made little sense when most colonists still considered themselves British; by his own account his warning was "The Regulars are coming out." William Dawes rode a separate route, and Dr. Samuel Prescott joined them. A British patrol stopped all three near Lincoln: Prescott escaped and reached Concord, Revere was captured. Henry Wadsworth Longfellow's 1860 poem "Paul Revere's Ride" made Revere the lone hero.

Myths you were taught in school, Part 2. What should I bust next?
